does: Seals food inside a shell of damp salt, so that it cooks in its own steam and is seasoned gently through its skin.

intro.what: Damp salt forms a firm shell around food with its skin left on.
intro.why: The shell contains steam. Understanding the barrier helps you distinguish the crust around the food from a coating meant to be eaten.

how: Mix coarse salt with enough egg white or water for it to feel like wet sand.
Spread a bed of the salt on a tray, lay the food on it with its skin on, and pack the rest of the salt over it until nothing shows.
Bake until the crust is hard and pale gold.
Push a thin probe through the crust into the thickest part and check it against a trusted guide to doneness.
Rest the food in its crust, then crack the shell, lift it off in pieces and brush away every loose grain before serving.

cues.text: The crust is hard and dry all over, and it sounds hollow when it is tapped.

mistakes.mistake: Scaling or skinning a fish first, so that the flesh takes up salt and turns harsh.
mistakes.fix: Leave the skin and the scales on. They keep the salt out.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving a gap in the crust, so that the steam escapes and the food dries.
mistakes.fix: Patch every crack with more damp salt before it goes into the oven.

quiz.question: What is the salt shell intended to contain?
choices: Hot dry air circulating directly over exposed flesh.
Extra salt intended to mix through the whole filling.
quiz.because: The enclosing shell keeps steam around the food instead of letting it escape freely.

quiz.question: How should the damp salt be packed before baking?
choices: Only beneath the food as a loose bed.
In scattered patches over exposed flesh.
Around the food with no exposed gaps.
quiz.because: A continuous shell provides the enclosure this method relies on.

quiz.question: What tells you that the shell itself has hardened?
choices: It looks dry and sounds hollow when tapped.
It still feels like loose damp sand.
It stays pliable and bends without cracking.
quiz.because: A hollow sound and a dry surface are cues about the texture of the salt shell.

quiz.question: A gap is visible before the tray enters the oven. What should you do?
choices: Leave it open as a steam vent.
Brush the gap with oil instead of closing it.
quiz.because: Closing gaps preserves the steam-containing shell.

variant_of.differs: The food is shut inside a shell of salt and steams there. Nothing browns.
